title: Savinho transfer: Spurs agree £85m deal to sign Brazi forward from Manchester City
author: Lyall Thomas; Michael Bridge
content:
Savinho transfer: Spurs agree £85m deal to sign Brazi forward from Manchester City
Savinho is set to undergo a medical ahead of a move to Tottenham Hotspur; Spurs have already spent more than £200m this summer on six first-team players; Savinho started in seven of his 24 Premier League appearances last season
Friday 21 August 2026 09:28, UK
Tottenham Hotspur have agreed an £85m deal with Manchester City to sign Savinho.
Spurs will pay an initial £75m for the Brazil international, with a further £10m available in add-ons.
It is understood £5m of the potential bonuses are effectively guaranteed, meaning City could receive at least £80m from the deal.
- Transfer Centre LIVE! | Tottenham news & transfers⚪
- Spurs fixtures & scores | FREE Spurs highlights▶️
- Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone📱
- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream PL games with no contract📺
Savinho is set to undergo a medical ahead of completing his move to north London.
Spurs are also continuing talks with Manchester City over a separate deal for striker Omar Marmoush as they look to strengthen their attacking options further.
Tottenham have already spent more than £200m on six first-team players this summer. They spent £185m on two midfielders, Sandro Tonali and Matheus Fernandes, from Newcastle and West Ham respectively.
Jan Paul van Hecke, meanwhile, joined from Brighton for £52m to replace Cristian Romero. Marcos Senesi, Andy Robertson and Martin Dubravka all arrived on free transfers.
Savinho, who has played a bit-part role since joining Manchester City in 2024, started only seven of his 24 Premier League appearances last season, in which he scored once and set up two goals.
How are Spurs spending so much money?
At the start of the transfer window, Sky Sports News' Michael Bridge explained how Spurs are able to spend big this summer...
"We're told there are absolutely no concerns about falling foul of the Premier League's financial rules.
"The club is in great financial health after qualifying for Europe in 18 of the last 20 seasons. The revenue driven by the stadium is huge: boxing, concerts, NFL games - you name it.
"In fact, in the Deloitte Money League, the rankings show that Tottenham Hotspur have leapfrogged Chelsea to become the ninth richest club in the world with annual revenues of £549.2m.
"On top of that, Spurs are one of the clubs to benefit most from the Premier League's shift to squad cost ratio from PSR, which has just come into effect. But the reason we're seeing Spurs spend so much is a shift in strategy under new leadership.
"Daniel Levy left at the start of last season, and there's a real desire to spend the money to dine at the very top table.
"Now the new leadership and the owners promised fans, after avoiding relegation on the final day, that they would spend the club's revenue on the first team, and they are delivering on that."
'City will want to replace Savinho and Marmoush'
Sky Sports News' Ben Ransom:
"Both players [Savinho and Marmoush] are essentially surplus to requirements at Manchester City. It's been pretty apparent through the summer. Enzo Maresca has said that in the case of both players, they are very much entitled to stay and fight for their first-team place.
"But equally he understands, a bit like James Trafford, when a player wants to play first-team football and they're not guaranteed the starting shirt, then the club, if they receive an offer that's acceptable, will not stand in their way. That applies to both players.
"City would need to replace these players. They would definitely, I'd say, have to replace one. They would like to and would aim to replace two.
"But the transfer window is closing in less than a fortnight. These are big positions to fill so late in the window."
summary: Tottenham Hotspur have agreed an £85m deal to sign Brazil forward Savinho from Manchester City, with the player set to undergo a medical. The transfer includes an initial £75m payment and £10m in add-ons, with £5m of those bonuses effectively guaranteed. This move follows Tottenham's heavy summer spending under new leadership, surpassing £200m on multiple first-team additions while maintaining strong financial health.
key_points: Spurs agreed an £85m fee for Savinho, consisting of £75m initially and £10m in add-ons.
Savinho is scheduled to undergo a medical ahead of his transfer to north London.
Tottenham have spent over £200m on six first-team players during the summer transfer window.
Savinho started only seven of his 24 Premier League appearances for Manchester City last season.

title: Arsenal Predictions: Opta Supercomputer’s Projections for Premier League 2026-27 | Opta Analyst
author: Matt Furniss
content:
How will Arsenal get on in the 2026-27 Premier League season? We look at the Opta supercomputer’s pre-season predictions for the defending champions.
Arsenal will begin a Premier League season as reigning champions for the first time in 22 years. The challenge now is simple: prove last season wasn’t a one off and continue to be dominant in the English top flight.
Pre-season expectations for the Gunners have only grown after a 3-0 demolition of Manchester City in the Community Shield last weekend. You may not read too much into that result considering only one of the previous 15 Community Shield winners has gone on to lift the Premier League trophy that season, but the manner of Arsenal’s performance against their nearest title rivals from last term was convincing, nonetheless.
Ahead of the opening game against Coventry City on Friday 21 August, we look at the Opta supercomputer’s pre-season projections for Arsenal in the Premier League.
The Opta Supercomputer’s Pre-Season Predictions
Most Likely Finish: 1st Place
Likelihood of Winning the Premier League: 40.6%
Likelihood of a Top-Four Finish: 80.3%
Arsenal are the Opta supercomputer’s pre-season favourites for the 2026-27 Premier League title, finishing in first place across 40.6% of its current 10,000 season simulations.
The Gunners have not successfully retained the top-flight title since 1935, when they became just the second club in English football history to win three successive league championships.
Mikel Arteta is now comfortably the long-serving manager in the Premier League after joining just under seven years ago (December 2019). He’s reinforced his squad with the important signings of Bruno Guimarães from Newcastle and creative winger Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge, while Aston Villa’s Ezri Konsa looks set to join soon.
Such is the Opta supercomputer’s confidence in Arsenal’s strengths, no other team in the Premier League won the 2026-27 title in more than a fifth of the pre-season simulations run today. Manchester City (19.6%) are deemed their closest challengers.
![Arsenal Predictions Premier League 2026-27](https://theanalyst.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/arsenal-predictions-premier-league-2026-27-1024x649.jpg)
With title rivals Man City, Chelsea and Liverpool all having new managers and Michael Carrick only just starting out as Manchester United’s permanent boss, there are a lot of question marks about what exactly to expect from those clubs in 2026-27.
As a result, the continuity at the Emirates Stadium boosts Arsenal’s pre-season confidence of back-to-back title wins.
Qualification for the UEFA Champions League looks very likely according to the supercomputer. Arsenal finished inside the top four in 80.3% of simulations – one of only two clubs in the Premier League to do so more often than not across the 10,000 season sims (alongside Man City – 60.1%).
If English clubs perform well in Europe again, then there is the possibility that fifth place will be enough for Champions League qualification too, with Arsenal’s projected chance of a top-five finish at 85.6%.
*All prediction data is based on Opta supercomputer projections from simulations run on 20 August 2026.

The Opta supercomputer heavily favors Arsenal to retain their title, giving them a 40.6% chance of finishing first and an 80.3% likelihood of a top-four finish. Manager Mikel Arteta's squad stability and new signings further bolster expectations, especially as rival clubs face uncertainty with new management.

The supercomputer projects an 80.3% likelihood that Arsenal will finish in the top four.
Arsenal has strengthened its squad under long-serving manager Mikel Arteta with key signings including Bruno Guimarães and Christos Tzolis.

title: England vs Pakistan: Harry Brook, Joe Root, Jordan Cox make runs in Headingley gloom
author: Stephan Shemilt
content:
Brook shines as England take control against Pakistan
- Published
First Rothesay Test, Headingley (day two of five)
Pakistan 171 all out: Shafique 61; Tongue 5-46, Robinson 5-51
England 366-8: Brook 91, Cox 73, Root 66; Usman 5-92
England are 195 runs ahead
Harry Brook sparkled in the Headingley gloom to build England's commanding lead over Pakistan on a shortened second day of the first Test.
Brook, overlooked for the Test captaincy, reinforced how important he will be to England's new era under Joe Root with a superb 91.
The vice-captain was crucially dropped on one and the reprieve allowed him to take England to 366-8, 195 ahead.
A stand of 120 with Dan Lawrence, who marked his recall with 51, came after Root and Jordan Cox both missed out on landmark centuries.
Root looked set to announce the beginning of his second spell as captain with a ton, while Cox was on course for a maiden hundred.
But their third-wicket partnership of 150 was ended when the impressive Cox feathered behind off the left-arm spin of Ali Usman for 73.
Four balls later, Root was left angry with himself by playing across the line to seamer Khurram Shahzad to be lbw for 66.
Nevertheless, Brook ensured England used the play possible on a damp, dank day in Leeds to cement their advantage.
Morning rain delayed the action until 14:45 BST. The clouds and floodlights should have given Pakistan the conditions to get back into the match. Instead, they could be beaten inside three days.
England dominate in Headingley gloom
England lose two quick wickets after 'poor' reviews
After England dismissed Pakistan for 171 and then moved to 112-2 by the end of the opening day, it seemed likely that their biggest barrier to significant progress on Thursday would be the weather.
And the elements were a challenge for all concerned. Umpire Allahuddien Paleker officiated in gloves, while England's backroom staff huddled on the dressing room balcony in thick coats.
The Pakistan seamers, ideally suited to the conditions, were presented with a golden opportunity. Instead, England were able to score at a Bazball-like rate of 4.5 runs per over, simply by tucking into the bad balls on offer.
Perhaps Pakistan would have made further inroads had captain Salman Ali Agha held Brook at second slip off Shahzad.
Had Brook been dismissed, England would have lost three wickets for seven runs. The score was 205-4 at the time, the hosts' lead 34, with only wicketkeeper Jamie Smith to come before the bowlers.
Thanks to the let-off, Brook treated his home crowd to strokeplay befitting his status as the number-one ranked batter in the world.
Maturing Brook underlines importance to new England
'Hometown boy' Brook reaches half-century
For some, Brook epitomised everything that was wrong with the Bazball era for his mistakes both on and off the field. This could have been his first Test as captain.
With or without the armband, he will be crucial to England's immediate prospects of success.
Speaking to BBC Sport last week, Brook acknowledged he had given some supporters cause for frustration. He admitted he is not the finished article as a Test batter and promised to work hard to recognise the right situations to unfurl his array of strokes.
The drop was an indeterminate stroke, a limp poke at Shahzad. After that, Brook played the situation beautifully.
He has a stellar record against Pakistan, and the tourists' attack did not have the weapons to trouble him â a plan for Mohammad Ali to bowl 78mph bouncers was dismissed with a savage pull for four.
It was not all brawn for Brook, who regularly played deft guides to third man. A century was there for the taking, only for a fatal error in the final half an hour before the close.
Trying to whip Usman into the leg side, Brook missed and was bowled. It is the second time in as many Tests he has been dismissed in the 90s on his home ground, following a 99 against India here last year.
Cox and Lawrence miss out on telling scores
Cox gets maiden Test half-century - best shots
While Brook's failure to register a ton is not a setback in the context of his career, Cox and Lawrence will reflect on the opportunities they had to make scores that would help establish them in this England side.
Injuries have meant Cox has had to wait for a sustained run in the team, with a chance at number three coming because of Jacob Bethell's knee problem. Lawrence is getting his fourth go at Test cricket, filling the void left by the retired Ben Stokes.
With Bethell set to come back when fit and the injured Sam Curran identified as a possible Stokes replacement, Cox and Lawrence have this series to make life tricky for the selectors. These innings, though both individually impressive, were not enough to make an irresistible case. Both men will need more.
From 23 not out overnight, Cox returned with the calmness he showed on Wednesday. He struck three fours in a single Shahzad over and moved to his first Test half-century by flicking Mohammad Abbas fine for four.
Cox should have been caught on 57 when he patted back to Shahzad. Perhaps the drop disrupted his concentration, because the wicket-taking delivery from Usman was innocuous. Cox simply followed one the left-armer got to turn and edged to the wicketkeeper.
Lawrence played on-drives off the seamers and sweeps off the spinners. One sweep too many at Usman resulted in a skied top-edge. After Usman removed Brook, he later accounted for Gus Atkinson and Ollie Robinson in successive balls for his maiden Test five-wicket haul.
All five of Usman's wickets
summary: England took control against Pakistan on a rain-affected second day of the first Test at Headingley, reaching 366-8 for a 195-run lead. Harry Brook led the charge with 91 runs, supported by Jordan Cox (73) and Dan Lawrence (51). Usman claimed five wickets for Pakistan, but England capitalized on favorable scoring conditions despite gloomy weather.
key_points: England closed day two at 366-8, holding a commanding 195-run lead over Pakistan.
Harry Brook top-scored with 91 after being dropped on one, while Jordan Cox and Dan Lawrence contributed 73 and 51 respectively.
Pakistan bowler Usman claimed a five-wicket haul, finishing with 5-92.
Morning rain delayed play until the afternoon on a gloomy, damp day at Headingley.

title: Carrick drops Rashford hint as Man Utd return approaches
author: Oli Gent
content:
![Add Evening Standard as a preferred source](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/google_preferred_source_badge_dark.png?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
![Harry Maguire sets his sights on winning more trophies with Manchester United](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/20/20/01M0DT3XN1B5HKMQT6YN35Q27N.jpg?width=1280&auto=webp&quality=75)
Rashford, 28, has not featured for his boyhood club since December 2024, where he fell out with then-manager Ruben Amorim.
He was subsequently shipped out on loan to Aston Villa for the remainder of that season, before he became part of the Portuguese’s ‘bomb squad’ in the summer last year.
Rashford then moved to Barcelona for the season on a loan with buy option deal, but the La Liga outfit decided against signing the winger permanently, despite some strong performances in Spain.
Now, he has been welcomed back to Old Trafford by Carrick, who has a decision to make as he prepares to oversee his first match as permanent head coach this weekend.
United travel to newly-promoted Hull City on Saturday lunchtime, and Rashford is in line to make the matchday squad after completing his comeback to the first-team fold last week.
The England star, who featured six times at this summer’s World Cup en route to the semi-finals, came off the substitutes’ bench in the Red Devils’ 4-2 defeat by AC Milan in Wroclaw, Poland, where United were beaten by their former coach, Amorim.
Questions remain over Rashford’s future at Old Trafford, with the transfer window open until September 1, but Carrick seems content to have him part of his squad this term.
"It has been pretty obvious that Marcus came back training with Kobbie [Mainoo] and Licha [Martinez] pretty much in Dublinl and that he has come back fantastically well,” Carrick said of him.
"He is enjoying his football, he looks fit, strong and looks ready to play football. I have been delighted with him since he came back.
"Of course, he can play through the middle, he has done. I wouldn't say it is naturally his No1 position, but he can do that.
Read More
"I think we have got forwards that give us that flexibility right across the frontline that we have used all of them pretty much in slightly different roles.
"I think for us to have that option is really good going through the season."
United have a conundrum up front with Benjamin Sesko returning back slowly from a shin problem that curtailed the end to his first season in England, while Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha can also operate as a central striker.
summary: Marcus Rashford has returned to Manchester United's first-team fold ahead of the new permanent head coach Michael Carrick's first match in charge against Hull City. Rashford spent time on loan at Aston Villa and Barcelona following a falling-out with former manager Ruben Amorim in December 2024. Carrick has praised Rashford's fitness and training attitude since his return, providing a valuable attacking option as the transfer window remains open.
key_points: Marcus Rashford has returned to Manchester United after loan spells at Aston Villa and Barcelona.
He is in line to make the matchday squad for Michael Carrick's first game as permanent head coach against Hull City.
Carrick praised Rashford's fitness, strong training performances, and positive attitude upon returning to the club.
Rashford provides tactical flexibility across the frontline amid other attacking options and fitness concerns for Benjamin Sesko.

title: Atlético Madrid offer Arsenal to Álvarez again: the player responds | Goal.com
author: Muhammad Sharaf Eldeen
content:
Atlético Madrid have changed their stance on the future of Argentine striker Julián Álvarez, opening the door to his departure during the current summer transfer window. But the Spanish club remain firm in one condition: no move to Barcelona.
According to the "Atletico Play" account, and confirmed by Catalan newspaper "Mundo Deportivo", Atlético have decided to open negotiations over Álvarez's sale after the striker made his desire to leave clear both inside and outside the club.
The Rojiblancos' management have attached one demand, though. His next destination must be Arsenal, who remain interested in signing him, and not Barcelona.
Read also
García a spectator and Hamza demands his right: "Sport" rates Barcelona's players against Al-Ahly
By video: violence at Camp Nou, Catalan police eject Al-Ahly fans
Álvarez, however, has no interest in Arsenal. He wants the Barcelona shirt, and nothing else, which leaves the deal at a dead end, according to "Mundo Deportivo".
Everything now hinges on how far each party is willing to hold its ground. Barcelona want a striker before the window shuts, and if they can't get one, they may push the deal back to January while continuing to chase Álvarez.
Atlético, for their part, have warmed to the idea of selling their star. But they need a replacement fast, and this is where Arsenal can help. Viktor Gyökeres has offered himself to a number of clubs, Barcelona included, and could be an acceptable option for Diego Simeone.
The biggest obstacle to all of this is Álvarez himself. He has left England and does not want to go back, which is exactly why he has already rejected the Gunners' offer.
Atlético's new proposal, the move to Arsenal, has only deepened the striker's frustration with his club. The relationship between the two sides has grown more strained, according to the Catalan newspaper.
You can discuss the topics and news in more depth in the "Kooora" forums.
summary: Atlético Madrid have opened the door to selling striker Julián Álvarez this summer, conditioning his departure on a move to Arsenal rather than Barcelona. However, Álvarez has rejected the offer because he wants to join Barcelona and does not want to return to England. This disagreement has created a dead end and strained the relationship between the player and the club.
key_points: Atlético Madrid are willing to sell Julián Álvarez during the summer transfer window.
Atlético's condition for the sale is that Álvarez must move to Arsenal instead of Barcelona.
Álvarez has rejected Arsenal's offer because he only wants to play for Barcelona and refuses to return to England.
The transfer standoff has increased tension and strained the relationship between Álvarez and the club management.

title: Manchester United Predictions: Opta Supercomputer’s Projections for Premier League 2026-27 | Opta Analyst
author: Jordan Collins
content:
How will Man Utd get on in the 2026-27 Premier League season? Can they build upon their impressive start under Michael Carrick? We look at the Opta supercomputer’s pre-season predictions.
Manchester United head into the 2026-27 Premier League season with a renewed sense of optimism. Michael Carrick’s rescue act last season has shifted the mood at Old Trafford from chaotic to calm and collected.
From Carrick’s appointment in January, United earned more points than every other Premier League team (39). That secured them a third-place finish in 2025-26 and qualification for the UEFA Champions League for the first time since 2022-23.
An overall positive pre-season combined with a smart transfer window will leave United’s supporters far more hopeful about this season.
Ahead of their opening game away against Hull City on Saturday 22 August, we look at the Opta supercomputer’s pre-season projections for United in the Premier League.
The Opta Supercomputer’s Pre-Season Predictions
Most Likely Finish: 3rd
Likelihood of Winning the Premier League: 6.6%
Likelihood of a Top Four Finish: 33.1%
The Opta supercomputer’s pre-season predictions show Manchester United as most likely to finish in third place in 2026-27 across its pre-season Premier League simulations. They secured that position in 9.6% of the 10,000 season sims.
Last season was only the fifth time the Red Devils have finished in the top three since the legendary Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013. In those thirteen seasons, United have been the fifth-best-performing team in the competition with 862 points, fewer than rivals Man City (1,096), Liverpool (1,007), Arsenal (951) and Chelsea (889).
Carrick, who was rewarded with a permanent two-year contract in May, now begins his first full campaign as head coach. He’s overseen a midfield rebuild this summer, with the signings of Andrey Santos from Chelsea and Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa, while Brighton’s Carlos Baleba looks set to complete the overhaul.
Club CEO Omar Berrada has said that United are looking to win the Premier League title within two years.
The Opta supercomputer does give them an outside chance of causing an upset this season, winning the Premier League title in 6.6% of its 10,000 pre-season simulations. To do that, they would need to fend off Arsenal (40.6%), Manchester City (19.6%) and Liverpool (9.2%), who all came out as more likely title-winners across the sims.
With many of the Premier League’s top sides having new managers, there are a lot of question marks about what exactly to expect from those clubs in 2026-27. That could potentially open the door for someone to cause a shock at the top.
![Man Utd Predictions Premier League 2026-27](https://theanalyst.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/man-utd-predictions-premier-league-2026-27-1024x649.jpg)
A minimum for United this season must be qualification for the Champions League, which is considered likely by the supercomputer. The Red Devils finished in a top-four spot in 33.1% of its pre-season simulations – with only Arsenal (80.4%), Man City (60.1%) and Liverpool (40.8%) doing so more often.
If English clubs perform well in Europe, then there is the possibility that fifth place would be unlocked for Champions League qualification. That’s happened in each of the last two seasons after the results by English clubs accumulated the most UEFA coefficient points. United’s projected chance of finishing in the top five places of the Premier League is 41.7%.
*All prediction data is based on Opta supercomputer projections from simulations run on 20 August 2026.

Subscribe to our football newsletter to receive exclusive weekly content. You can also follow our social accounts over on X, Instagram, TikTok and Facebook.

summary: Following a successful conclusion to the 2025-26 season under manager Michael Carrick, Manchester United enters the 2026-27 Premier League campaign with renewed optimism. The Opta supercomputer projects United to finish third in the league, giving them a 6.6% chance of winning the title and a 33.1% likelihood of a top-four finish. The club has bolstered its squad with summer midfield signings as they look to build upon their qualification for the UEFA Champions League.
key_points: Michael Carrick was rewarded with a permanent two-year contract in May after leading United to a third-place finish and Champions League qualification last season.
The Opta supercomputer predicts Manchester United's most likely finish for the 2026-27 season is third place.
United are given a 6.6% chance of winning the Premier League title and a 33.1% likelihood of securing a top-four finish.
The club's summer transfer activity includes midfield additions such as Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans.

title: Arteta demands ‘desire and ambition’ for title defence and says Lewis-Skelly will stay
author: Ed Aarons
content:
Mikel Arteta has called on Arsenal to prove they have the desire to defend their Premier League title on the eve of the new season. He also reiterated that Myles Lewis-Skelly will not be leaving in this transfer window.
Arsenal face Coventry in their opening match on Friday night as they attempt to retain the championship for the first time since the 1930s. Arsenal have won 17 of their past 18 matches against promoted teams and have not been beaten at the Emirates Stadium by one since November 2010 – a run of 45 matches.
While Arsenal are heavy favourites to start with a comfortable victory, especially after their impressive win over Manchester City in the Community Shield on Sunday, Arteta believes they must adapt to a different challenge this time.
“We need to take this organically because it’s going to be a long marathon,” he said. “What we need to show is that desire and ambition to be better than we were last season, a month ago, or a week ago when we played Man City. We have the ability to improve, to evolve, and that’s what I sense and I feel around the club and especially around the players.”
Asked whether Arsenal begin the season with a target on their backs, he said: “Today, no, because we start from scratch and we’re going to have to prove we have the level to go back to that position again.
“But that happened in the last three seasons – at some point we were first, at some point we were chasing it, and you never know what’s better.
“You give me the choice, I want to be first, I want to be hunted, and I want to be in control of our future, rather than depending on somebody else.”
It is understood Myles Lewis-Skelly was offered to Manchester United and Chelsea as Arsenal attempt to raise funds after the £75m purchase of Bruno Guimarães from Newcastle. The 19-year-old academy graduate was outstanding in midfield against City in Cardiff, having also started in that position in the Champions League final last season against Paris Saint-Germain, and Arteta is “100%” confident he will remain at Arsenal.
“The players that have been raised in our system, and they feel that love and that connection with the club, bring something else, there’s no question about that,” he said. “We need to look after them in a really special way because they bring value that is very difficult to find. That’s why, when we can, we want to protect those assets as much as possible, develop them and make them extremely important for the club.”
Arteta said Martín Zubimendi remains an integral part of his squad and he expects the midfielder to remain despite reported interest from Real Madrid.
after newsletter promotion
Zubimendi was outstanding for most of last season before losing his place to Lewis-Skelly, but Arteta said he has reassured the Spain international that he still has a big role to play at the club “I had various conversations with him. First of all, for him to understand my decisions, he knew perfectly where they were coming from and he’s an extremely honest and straight guy. He’s so demanding of himself that sometimes it can be too much.
“But he knows that and he knew that we were going to add and increase the quality of the squad. Because it has to happen in every position and we cannot not do what we did.
“When he got to the last stage of his season, he already played 55 games. We cannot have that again at this level. He recognises that. Now it’s going to be: ‘OK, how I’m going to now raise the level to be able to do what I did last year. But for 11 months.’”
summary: Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has called on his team to show desire and ambition as they prepare to defend their Premier League title, starting with a match against Coventry. Arteta also confirmed that 19-year-old academy graduate Myles Lewis-Skelly will stay at the club during the transfer window. Additionally, Arteta stated that midfielder Martín Zubimendi remains an integral part of the squad despite reported interest from Real Madrid.
key_points: Mikel Arteta demanded desire and ambition from Arsenal ahead of their Premier League title defence.
Arsenal open their season with a match against Coventry at the Emirates Stadium.
Arteta is 100% confident that Myles Lewis-Skelly will not leave the club this transfer window.
Arteta expects Martín Zubimendi to remain at Arsenal despite interest from Real Madrid.

title: Premier League returns and Arsenal sense opportunity with rivals in flux
author: David Hytner
content:
Mikel Arteta wants to get his messaging absolutely right. According to him, Arsenal are not about to defend their Premier League title. They are set to attack another one.
Remember Win the dog, who the manager brought in to the club’s training ground a few years back? She must now be called “Won”. But it is when Arteta quibbles over another bout of semantics that he highlights why he is entering the new season with such energy and optimism.
Do not talk to him about Arsenal’s stability. He prefers the word “consistency” along with more thrusting ones like “ambition”. The overall theme is clear. When Arteta surveys the landscape at the top end of the English game, he sees a settled environment at his club and flux elsewhere.
In terms of the so-called Big Six – the richest clubs in the country, as ranked by Deloitte – there are new managers at Manchester City, Liverpool and Chelsea; a virtually new one at Tottenham and a relatively new one at Manchester United. It has been a summer of unprecedented change in the Premier League with nine clubs with a new man in charge. Of those who hold out hope of a title challenge, only Aston Villa have a fully bedded-in manager in Unai Emery.
Rather abruptly, Arteta finds himself as the longest-serving manager in the division; he took over from Emery at Arsenal in December 2019. Emery is second on the list, having been at Villa for three years and nine months, and only one other – Daniel Farke at Leeds – has been at his club for more than three years.
When Arteta was given the job at Arsenal, Pep Guardiola was two titles into his storied City tenure, Jürgen Klopp had won the Champions League at Liverpool and was on his way to winning the league that season and José Mourinho had just joined Spurs.
![Mikel Arteta holds the Premier League trophy](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/d8c26acdcf196fcb29878c727d9df1151b19c423/0_0_8192_5464/master/8192.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Arteta has seen them all off, with Guardiola’s departure from City at the end of last season being the most significant single shift in the dynamics for the forthcoming campaign.
Arteta is now the big beast, the only current manager to have won the Premier League, and as Arsenal prepare for the curtain-raiser at home to Coventry on Friday night, it is hard to ignore the confidence they are projecting. With virtually of all their rivals in transition, uncertainty undercutting the excitement, predictions difficult to make in the face of little actual evidence, Arsenal are reassured by their firm foundations. They sense opportunity, another title; the creation of a dynasty. That is the ultimate goal.
There is something more. Namely how everything changed for them in the closing weeks of last season. City had done the hard work, clawing back a nine-point deficit from the middle of March – a period when they had a game in hand. But in the five-match shootout that followed, City blinked first, drawing at Everton. Most know how nerve-racking it was for Arsenal. Not least Arteta. The Emirates Stadium was a sea of anxiety when Arsenal last played there – against Burnley in the penultimate game of the season. They got a 1-0 win over the line.
![Bruno Guimarães on the ball against Manchester City](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/e50b2b463f1a38c779db11f3544de56b9e706617/0_0_3765_2510/master/3765.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Then City drew at Bournemouth and it was over; Arsenal’s 22-year wait, the oppressive weight. It is impossible to underestimate the feeling of liberation. Nobody can question the bottle of this team. Nobody will taunt them with the cry of “second again, olé, olé.” It is plain Arteta and his players will feed off it and perhaps it will lead to a more expansive style of football. The fear of falling short inhibited their game as the heat rose last time out.
Arsenal have made changes behind the scenes, looking for the marginal gains, most notably in the medical department where the head doctor, Zafar Iqbal, was mutually consented in early June. Arnaldo Abrantes has come in from Aston Villa to replace him. If the players can stay fitter for longer, Arsenal believe they can stay ahead. They have protected themselves with moves to deepen an already well-stocked squad. Bruno Guimarães is the most eye-catching addition, with Ezri Konsa about to follow.
Arsenal versus City still feels like the primary head-to-head. Guardiola had Arteta’s number last season, winning two and drawing one of the three meetings between the clubs. City were much the better team in the Carabao Cup final that they won 2-0. But that was under Guardiola and that was with Rodri and Bernardo Silva. If Guardiola’s exit has hit City the hardest, then those of the commanding midfielders to Barcelona and Real Madrid, respectively, is not far behind.
City’s faith in their new manager, Enzo Maresca, is rooted in what they saw of him when he worked on their coaching staff; he was an assistant to Guardiola in the treble-winning season of 2022-23. Previously, he coached the Under‑23s to the Premier League 2 title in 2020-21.
![Elliot Anderson shakes hands with Manchester City supporters](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/7359604bb5bf08fa1e83a25f41e9a4c5e28ed584/0_0_4556_2984/master/4556.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
It is a well-thought-through appointment; the kind a well-run club makes. Yet at the same time, it is not one to quicken the pulse. Maresca, quite simply, has enormous shoes to fill. Ditto Elliot Anderson, the impressive young midfielder upon whom City have bet the house. Can City be better given the personnel losses they have sustained? They must surely do so given the direction of travel at Arsenal. City do retain the cheat code that is Erling Haaland.
There are parallels between City and Liverpool, who want their new manager, Andoni Iraola, to have a similar impact in his first season that Arne Slot managed in 2024-25. Slot took Klopp’s team and glided to the title. Maybe consistency in the dugout is not everything?
On the other hand, Slot was given only one new player – Federico Chiesa – who barely played that season and he essentially stuck with what had made the Klopp collective so successful. It was evolution not revolution. When he tried the latter last season, Slot found that his tenure unravelled, although his rotten luck with injuries must be acknowledged. There was also the death of Diogo Jota.
after newsletter promotion
Liverpool have moved on Andy Robertson, Ibrahima Konaté and, most crucially, Mohamed Salah, even if he was a shadow of his former self last season. Salah has not yet been replaced; it would be impossible to replace the prime-years version of him and Iraola, who has a number of injury concerns, has it all to do.
Coaxing more from Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak is fundamental. Iraola’s style has the capacity to hold Anfield in thrall; the aggression, the front-foot slickness, the boldness to go one-versus-one all over the pitch. How quickly can he impose it?
Chelsea will be interesting under Xabi Alonso, who has been allowed to add players to fit into the 3-4-2-1 he used to such stunning effect at Bayer Leverkusen. Alonso has also been permitted to break from the club’s youth-first signing model and bring in much-needed experience.
![Morgan Rogers celebrates scoring](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/88830c50f28c36d7c26f7e89744f03ce1fea2b00/0_0_5023_3349/master/5023.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Morgan Rogers, alongside Cole Palmer and behind João Pedro, with Moisés Caicedo and maybe Reece James in the deep midfield roles, has a very nice feel to it. There is talent in central defence. The lack of European football will be a temporary blessing.
Ask any chief executive what supporters want at the start of a season and the answer is invariably the same: be better than last season. Which will not be a problem for Chelsea after the implosion to limp home in 10th. Or Spurs, who finished 17th for the second campaign in a row and narrowly avoided relegation. Roberto De Zerbi, who was appointed as the manager with seven games to go, kept them up and in the first summer since the end of Daniel Levy’s near 25-year as chair, the new hierarchy have been determined to act decisively. Their heavy spend on Premier League-proven players has allowed the fanbase to dream.
De Zerbi is a man to generate buy-in. In him they trust. Ditto a midfield that will feature Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes. With Conor Gallagher or James Maddison expected to fill the No 10 role, Spurs look to have a proper unit to hold things together. They will also benefit from no European football.
What about United, for whom everything suddenly came together after the appointment of Michael Carrick in January, initially for an interim spell? His record meant the club had to give him the job on a permanent basis – he finished the season with 12 wins and three draws from 17 league matches. It was 2.3 points per game. Transpose that over a 38-match campaign and you get 87 points. Arsenal won the title with 85. Are United dark horses for glory?
Concerns remain. Carrick was largely untroubled by injuries and when United have their best XI on the field they are a match for anybody. When they miss a few, as they normally did under Ruben Amorim, they can flatline. United were always going to have to add a good number of signings this summer, particularly as they prepare to go from a Europe-free season to a return to the Champions League. They have not yet done enough; the final week-and-a-half of the transfer window could be crucial. As Mike Tyson almost said, everybody has a plan until they are punched in the face by the Champions League.
![Marcus Rashford runs](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/da859f9e4aab2120f242f6f8f0ecbb29fc4a877b/0_0_5000_3333/master/5000.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Are Villa really about to take another step forward after the highs of last season when they finished fourth and won the Europa League? It feels unlikely given the departures, headlined by those of Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, with Konsa primed to go, too. Strangely, there is a whiff of transition about them. It is possible to find reasons to fret about every team. Apart from Arsenal.
summary: As the Premier League returns, Arsenal enter the new season with high confidence, firm foundations, and a settled squad under Mikel Arteta. In contrast, many of their traditional rivals among the Big Six are experiencing a summer of unprecedented change with new managers and squad transitions. Arsenal sense a major opportunity to attack another title and build a dynasty following the relief and liberation of ending their long title drought last season.
key_points: Mikel Arteta is now the longest-serving and only current manager in the division to have previously won the Premier League.
Arsenal's rivals face widespread transition, with new managers taking charge at Manchester City, Liverpool, Chelsea, Tottenham, and Manchester United.
Arsenal have strengthened their squad and medical department in pursuit of marginal gains and deeper squad depth.
Manchester City face a period of adjustment following the departure of Pep Guardiola and key midfielders.
Other top clubs like Liverpool, Chelsea, Tottenham, and Manchester United enter the season with varying degrees of uncertainty and managerial changes.

title: Rangers: Derek McInnes' side serve up stodgy 12-course banquet of huff and puff
author: Tom English
content:
![Derek McInnes](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2048/cpsprodpb/1537/live/1ecc22c0-9ce3-11f1-9e72-05a4f32fdb83.jpg)
Derek McInnes recorded his second win in two games, but it was far from straightforward
- Published
Of all the dullness on display at Ibrox, Cammy Devlin's five-minute cameo stood apart. A blink-and-you'll-miss-him appearance from a substitute who was supposed to be a leader, a senior man, a guy to nurse Rangers to the endgame with their flimsy 1-0 lead intact.
Devlin's night ended with a deserved red card for a ridiculous and entirely needless lunge that fried the brain.
The midfielder was brought to Rangers to add steel, not to contribute to the mental frailties that dogged them on the run-in last season. He was meant to be part of the solution, not at risk of being part of the problem.
The red could have put Rangers' win in jeopardy, had Jablonec been up to much, which they weren't. They were organised but unthreatening. They were committed but lacked much resembling a goal threat.
They were creative only in their histrionics and their survival tactics. You haven't seen such swooning since the golden age of the Hollywood diva.
Rangers should put them out of the competition next week. Should. There are no guarantees. Derek McInnes is experienced and wily and hard working, but his team is not a smart team, not yet anyhow.
They're not coached to find space, to drag defences out of shape and then hit them hard. They're workmanlike in the main. Honest, but awfully lacking in inspiration.
It was Rangers' job to come up with the creativity to break Jablonec down and what a meal they made of it. A 12-course banquet of huff and puff finally brought to an end by one of the few bouts of coherent football that led to Ryan Naderi's winner.
The positives won't take long. A one-goal lead to take to Jablonec next week; a clean-sheet; industry from Djeidi Gassama and James Penrice; assured defending from Olwethu Makhanya; signs of improvement in Naderi; a full-time whistle not accompanied by booing, as the half-time whistle had been.
It was a tough watch, though. Rangers in that first half lacked movement and cleverness and X-factor. They were an eyesore. Time and again, defenders looked downfield for a pass to hit only to see their team-mates looking back at them, unmoving and tightly marked.
Poor old Emmanuel Fernandez had another difficult experience but there were times when you had sympathy for him.
Wanting to be positive in possession and play forward, he had no options, nowhere to go but back, which drew groans of derision. When he gambled with a risky ball and failed to find a target, there was another uprising. Angry, angry, angry.
He gestured at one point, a waved arm that suggested he wasn't over-burdened with runners ahead of him.
McInnes spent much of his night walking madly about his technical area. That's a confined space, but his step count will have been stratospheric. He probably crashed through the 10,000 steps in 15 minutes. Perhaps he needs help, another coach with a different skill-set, new and more imaginative thinking.
![Graphic](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1200/cpsprodpb/da91/live/5296e2a0-9ce5-11f1-aed2-8d6da8d75094.png)
Rangers have spent fortunes... but badly
You took all of this in and wondered what Andrew Cavenagh must have been making of it in America.
Eleven new signings in recent weeks and close to 30 since his consortium moved in last summer. Their running total of transfer fees long since careered past the Â£25m mark. Last January, it sped across the Â£35m barrier and now it's knocking on the door of Â£50-Â£60m on new players.
These players. These largely dull, pedestrian Rangers men playing in front of a mostly hushed and increasingly tired stadium with 15,000 empty seats. They won on the night, and so hope lives for some of kind of European story this season, but it was so desperately lacking.
Within the club there is patience and a mindset that this is a long road Rangers are on and an acceptance they're only at the start of it.
There is a commitment to spend and spend again. Cavenagh and his backers have been true to their word, they have stumped up fortunes. Have they spent well? Right now, it's impossible to say that they have.
McInnes on narrow victory in Conference League play-off
Compare this to Celtic's elan and fluidity the night before. Compare the sustained class of Camilo Duran to anything that Rangers have. Duran cost somewhere between five and six million.
Where is Rangers' Duran? Where is their Callum McGregor, their Benjamin Nygren, their Kieran Tierney, their standard-setters, their goal machines, their players who drive the team forward?
Where, indeed, is their Nico Raskin? On the bench on the night. Unused. A wee injury, apparently. Nothing to do with the rumoured gathering interest from Fenerbahce, we were told.
The rumour-machine was in overdrive in pre-match. Is he going? How much is he going for? Who's coming in? Where's he coming in from?
The plates continue to spin at Ibrox as McInnes attempts to put order on all of this, to forge a coherent team from all the disparate parts.
He has to make it work against a backdrop of Celtic threatening to run amok with what they already have and what they might soon add if the Â£40m of Champions League loot drops into their lap next week.
An hour after the final whistle, the only sound heard at Ibrox was the hum of three lawnmowers gliding over the turf. It was quiet, eerily so.
You half wondered if McInnes might come out for a moment just to experience how calm it can be out there. Take it while he can. There won't be much stillness in this place for a while yet.
summary: Derek McInnes secured his second consecutive win as Rangers manager with a narrow 1-0 victory over Jablonec, courtesy of Ryan Naderi's late winner. Despite the clean sheet and the first-leg lead, the performance was widely criticized as dull, uninspired, and lacking in creativity. Substitute Cammy Devlin also received a red card late in the match for a needless challenge, highlighting ongoing disciplinary and mental concerns within the squad.
key_points: Ryan Naderi scored the decisive goal to give Rangers a 1-0 lead heading into the second leg against Jablonec.
Substitute Cammy Devlin was deservedly sent off late in the match for a needless lunge.
Rangers have spent heavily on numerous new signings under their current ownership, but critics question whether the funds have been spent well given the team's pedestrian performances.
The team struggled with a lack of movement, creativity, and forward options during a difficult first half.

title: Harry Brook keeps England well on top of Pakistan in first Test despite late wickets
author: Ali Martin
content:
The clock had just ticked past 7pm, there was still half an hour of play left on this soggy second day, and it looked for all money that Harry Brook would end a year-long wait for his 11th Test century with a first at his home ground of Headingley.
Brook had agonisingly missed out by one run against India here last summer. And this time, against a ragged Pakistan side that had handed him a life second ball amid another outing to forget, the box was practically begging to be ticked.
And then it happened. With 91 runs to his name, Brook rocked back and went to push the left-arm spin of Ali Usman through vacant midwicket only to swipe at fresh air and hear the ball cannon on to his stumps. Brook came into this match as the world’s No 1-ranked batter but this particular local peak remains elusive.
For all that Brook was cursing himself back in the dressing room, and Usman struck twice more before stumps – he ended the day with five for 92 – it was not hugely damaging to England’s position. At stumps Joe Root’s side had progressed to 366 for eight, and a lead of 195 runs, with victory inside three days not beyond the realms of possibility.
Saying as much is dangerous at a ground famous for its turnarounds, likewise against a team with a history of producing the unexpected. But across the 57 overs of play that were possible, as Root (66), Jordan Cox (73), and Dan Lawrence (51) similarly made unconverted half-centuries, it was hard to be upbeat about the tourists.
It was already looking a long way back for Pakistan after that ruinous first day at the hands of Ollie Robinson and Josh Tongue. But with a night’s sleep, and rain halting the match until 2.45pm, they had time to regroup; time to think about what caused their own dismissals before harnessing helpful conditions themselves.
![Jordan Cox holds the bottom of his bat to his face](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/b1023fadd5021020221b79133d17055f50d0a665/0_0_2176_1354/master/2176.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Unfortunately a side that came into this series amid low expectations managed to somehow fall short of even these. Across the two overcast sessions, floodlights at full beam, their quicks failed to match Robinson’s relentless line and length, chances went begging, and their ground fielding was borderline slapstick.
Summing it up was Usman trying to stop a boundary with his boot at one stage and kicking it over the rope. Unathletic as this was, at least Usman was trying to cut off the boundary. At times this seemed beneath Mohammad Abbas and Mohammad Ali, two men who would doubtless expect better off their own bowling.
The daft thing was, Pakistan actually had a sniff here. Root and Cox had looked largely untroubled after resuming on 112 for two, a stand of 150 pushing England past parity and into the lead. Cox in particular looked so assured in his second Test, the new No 3 owning the space and feasting on a string of freebies.
But when both men fell in successive overs against the run of play – Cox edging Usman behind, Root trapped lbw falling over to the previously wayward Khurram Shahzhad – England were suddenly four wickets down, just 31 runs ahead. Here was an opportunity that Pakistan simply had to grasp.
The same went for the wafted edge that Brook immediately sent into the slip cordon second ball, only for the stand-in skipper, Salman Ali Agha, to dive across Imam-ul-Haq and put it down. Agha left the field for treatment – embarrassment may have played a part here – and Brook scarcely looked back thereafter.
after newsletter promotion
At the other end was Lawrence, a player handed another stab at Test cricket after becoming collateral damage during the Bazball experiment, and between them they put on 120 more runs for the fifth wicket. Usman was getting grip from the surface but struggled with control, while Pakistan’s medium-fast seamers continued to toil.
A further opportunity came and went for Pakistan here, and once again the upshot was high farce. Lawrence danced down to Usman on 37 and was struck on the pad, with the rebound presenting Agha with a chance to run him out from slip. But the throw crashed into Mohammad Rizwan’s back as the wicketkeeper continued his appeal for lbw. Better awareness might have seen him get out of the way.
![Harry Brook is bowled by Pakistan’s Ali Usman](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/b8e4f4aeb63f5812e42dd467f255182030aaa638/0_0_4294_2759/master/4294.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Lawrence eventually fell trying to mow Usman over cow corner and sending it skywards off the top edge, the latest in a string of anticlimactic moments in the gloom. Root could have started his second stint as captain with a century, while the effervescent Cox could have announced himself to the world.
But none of these near-misses compared to the collective sigh that met Brook’s late dismissal. For all that he took just 55 balls to make his half-century, and had just faced 93 by the time Usman hit the timber, Brook had played a mature knock, guiding his 13 fours, rather than trying to smoke them, and looking switched on.
Despite being the best pitch in the country, and a place positively dripping in history, somehow this is Headingley’s last men’s Test match until 2029. Unless Pakistan can deliver the unthinkable with the bat second time around, Brook’s wait for a century on his home ground is going to be a long one.
summary: England maintained a strong position against Pakistan on the second day of the first Test at Headingley, reaching 366 for eight with a 195-run lead. Harry Brook starred with 91 runs before being bowled by Ali Usman, who claimed five wickets for 92 runs. Despite missed opportunities and late wickets from Pakistan, England remains well on top with a potential victory in sight.
key_points: Harry Brook was bowled for 91 by Ali Usman, missing out on a century at his home ground of Headingley.
England finished the rain-affected second day at 366 for eight, holding a 195-run lead.
Joe Root (66), Jordan Cox (73), and Dan Lawrence (51) all contributed unconverted half-centuries for England.
Ali Usman finished the day with five wickets for 92 runs for Pakistan, supported by late breakthroughs.
Pakistan struggled with missed chances and poor fielding throughout the day's play.

title: England vs Pakistan: Harry Brook misses out on century as Joe Root, Jordan Cox, and Dan Lawrence impress in dominant batting performance
author: Noah Langford
content:
England vs Pakistan: Harry Brook misses out on century as Joe Root, Jordan Cox, and Dan Lawrence impress in dominant batting performance
Harry Brook missed out on a century on his home ground after notching a masterful 91 off 93 balls; Jordan Cox, Joe Root, and Dan Lawrence all made fifties; Usman Tariq took five-fer; watch day three from 10.15am Friday on Sky Sports Cricket and Sky Sports Main Event
Thursday 20 August 2026 20:04, UK
Harry Brook missed out on a century after notching 91 from 93 balls in a masterful innings that headlined a dominant England batting performance against Pakistan on day two of the first Test at Headingley.
Brook (91 off 93) led the charge and was aided by big scores from Jordan Cox (73), returning captain Joe Root (66), and Dan Lawrence (51) to consolidate what turned into a mammoth 195-run lead for England, as they ended the day on 366-8 in reply to Pakistan's 171.
The struggling visiting attack was only able to bowl 58 overs after a rain-sodden morning delayed all play until 2:45pm.
No 1 ranked Test batter Brook was clean bowled by the brilliant Usman Tariq (5-91), consigning him to missing out on triple figures at his home ground in a Test for the second summer running, after notching a stunning 99 off 112 against India last June.

His nonetheless impressive work with the bat, though, means England are well on their way to victory against a Pakistan side staring down the barrel of their ninth defeat in 12 Tests.

title: Man Utd confirm transfer target for remainder of window after Carlos Baleba twist
author: Tashan Deniran-Alleyne
content:

With the Red Devils are expected to get a deal - worth around £65million - for the Cameroon international over the line, Carrick has revealed United will remain active in the window all the way up until transfer Deadline Day.
